code_quality.title: Extract duplicated batch operation views into reusable utility
code_quality.description: The functions `production_order_batch_start` and `production_order_batch_complete` in apps/production/views.py are nearly identical (~75 lines each). They share the same JSON parsing logic, validation, atomic transaction pattern, error handling, and response formatting. Only the action method (start vs complete) and response messages differ.
code_quality.rationale: This duplication violates the DRY principle and increases maintenance burden. Any bug fix or enhancement needs to be applied twice. A generic batch operation utility would reduce code by ~60 lines and make it easier to add new batch operations in the future.
code_quality.currentState: Two near-identical functions (production_order_batch_start and production_order_batch_complete) with 75+ lines each, differing only in the action method called and success/failure messages.
code_quality.proposedChange: Create a generic `batch_operation_handler` utility function that accepts: the model class, the action method name, success/failure message templates, and the request. Both batch start and batch complete views would become thin wrappers calling this utility.
code_quality.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - extract common logic into reusable utilities

code_quality.title: Extract modal components from large template files
code_quality.description: The template file templates/production/bin_list.html has 1110 lines, with approximately 400+ lines dedicated to modal dialogs (Create Bin Modal, Load Bin Modal, Empty Bin Modal, Batch Create Modal, Batch Print Modal). Similar patterns exist in other large templates like production_order_list.html (910 lines) and reservations_list.html (726 lines).
code_quality.rationale: Large template files are difficult to navigate, maintain, and test. The modal components are self-contained and could be reused across different views. Extracting them would improve template organization and enable better reuse of UI patterns.
code_quality.currentState: Multiple templates over 700+ lines with inline modal definitions that repeat similar patterns (form structure, button layout, loading states). The project already has a templates/components/ directory with reusable components like _modal.html, _pagination.html, _form_field.html.
code_quality.proposedChange: Extract modal templates into reusable components: templates/production/modals/_bin_create.html, _bin_load.html, _bin_empty.html, _batch_create.html, _batch_print.html. Use Django's {% include %} tag with context variables for customization.
code_quality.codeExample: {% include 'production/modals/_bin_create.html' with warehouses=warehouses %} {% include 'production/modals/_bin_load.html' with materials=materials %} {% include 'production/modals/_batch_print.html' with templates=templates printers=printers %}
code_quality.bestPractice: Component-based architecture - break large files into smaller, reusable pieces
prerequisites: Review existing templates/components/ directory for patterns to follow

code_quality.title: Add pre-commit hooks for automated code quality checks
code_quality.description: The project has excellent linting configuration in pyproject.toml (ruff, mypy, bandit) but lacks pre-commit hooks to automatically run these checks before commits. This means developers must manually run linting, which often gets skipped.
code_quality.rationale: Pre-commit hooks provide automated enforcement of code quality standards, catching issues before they enter the codebase. Without them, code style and quality can drift over time as developers forget to run manual checks.
code_quality.currentState: Ruff, mypy, and bandit are configured in pyproject.toml but there's no .pre-commit-config.yaml file. Code quality checks must be run manually.
code_quality.proposedChange: Add a .pre-commit-config.yaml file that runs ruff (linting + formatting), mypy (type checking), and bandit (security) automatically on staged files before each commit.
code_quality.codeExample:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.8.0
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format
  
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
    rev: v1.13.0
    hooks:
      - id: mypy
        additional_dependencies: [django-stubs]
  
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/bandit
    rev: 1.8.0
    hooks:
      - id: bandit
        args: [-c, pyproject.toml]
code_quality.bestPractice: Shift-left quality - catch issues as early as possible in the development cycle
prerequisites: Ensure all existing code passes ruff checks first to avoid blocking commits

code_quality.title: Move inline json imports to module level
code_quality.description: Multiple view files import the `json` module inside function bodies rather than at the top of the file. This pattern appears in apps/production/views.py (lines 177, 254, 890), apps/inventory/views.py (lines 816, 1090, 1162), and apps/inventory/views/reservation_views.py (lines 89, 161).
code_quality.rationale: Importing modules inside functions is unconventional Python style and slightly less efficient (though negligible). More importantly, it obscures dependencies and makes it harder to see what a module depends on at a glance. PEP 8 recommends imports at the top of files.
code_quality.currentState: The `import json` statement appears inside function bodies in 7+ locations across view files, typically at the start of AJAX handler functions.
code_quality.proposedChange: Move all `import json` statements to the top of each file with other imports. The json module is part of Python's standard library and has minimal import overhead.
code_quality.bestPractice: PEP 8 - Imports should usually be on separate lines at the top of the file

code_quality.title: Split production models.py into domain-specific model files
code_quality.description: The file apps/production/models.py contains 747 lines with 5 distinct model classes: ProductionOrder, Bin, BinHistory, Batch, and BatchItem. While these models are related, they represent distinct domain concepts with their own responsibilities and methods.
code_quality.rationale: Large model files become difficult to navigate and maintain. Splitting into separate files improves code organization, makes it easier to find and modify specific models, and reduces merge conflicts when multiple developers work on different models.
code_quality.currentState: Single 747-line file containing 5 model classes: ProductionOrder (~100 lines), Bin (~220 lines), BinHistory (~100 lines), Batch (~210 lines), BatchItem (~60 lines)
code_quality.proposedChange: Split into separate model files: apps/production/models/production_order.py, apps/production/models/bin.py (containing Bin and BinHistory), apps/production/models/batch.py (containing Batch and BatchItem). Create apps/production/models/__init__.py to re-export all models for backwards compatibility.
code_quality.codeExample:
# apps/production/models/__init__.py
from .production_order import ProductionOrder
from .bin import Bin, BinHistory
from .batch import Batch, BatchItem

__all__ = ['ProductionOrder', 'Bin', 'BinHistory', 'Batch', 'BatchItem']

# apps/production/models/bin.py
from django.db import models
from apps.core.models import BaseModel

class Bin(BaseModel):
    # ... Bin model definition

class BinHistory(BaseModel):
    # ... BinHistory model definition
code_quality.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each file should have one clear purpose
prerequisites: Ensure all imports of production models are updated to use the new structure
